assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices, and the associated dynamic-industry framework, changed how economists measure demand, market power, merger effects and welfare. The methods are used throughout industrial organisation, antitrust practice and adjacent fields such as trade and health. The work combines economic theory, identification and computation, and it has produced credible, replicable empirical results.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is the Berry (1994) inversion, BLP (1995) and Pakes' related work on estimation and dynamic games. Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes carry the central demand-estimation credit. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin made distinct contributions that a three-person cap would leave out.
assessment.maturity: About thirty years of continuous use and extension. The approach is a standard tool, and its practical value has been confirmed repeatedly. The timing is mature and no further confirmation is needed.
uncertainties: The three-person limit excludes Bresnahan and Reiss, whose claim to the empirical-IO revolution is also substantial.
The credit split between the demand-side (BLP) and dynamic-game (Pakes) strands is a judgment call.
I am relying on my own knowledge of the field; I did not verify sources independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore's 'Credit Cycles' model shows how collateral constraints turn small shocks into large, persistent fluctuations through the feedback between asset prices and borrowing capacity. It is one of the most influential macro-financial mechanisms, and it was central to post-2008 research and policy thinking on financial amplification.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 paper is the clear origin of the collateral-feedback mechanism and is clearly credited to Kiyotaki and Moore. Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist developed the related financial accelerator, and this is a separate and complementary strand. A two-person prize for the collateral mechanism is clean.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is now canonical in graduate macroeconomics. Its relevance was confirmed by the global financial crisis and by a large literature on financial frictions.
uncertainties: The relationship to Bernanke's 2022 recognition and to the Gertler-linked financial accelerator may reduce the perceived marginal novelty.
Some of the empirical validation of the mechanism is indirect and model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Obstfeld and Rogoff built the intertemporal, microfounded framework for open-economy macroeconomics (the 'redux' model and their textbook). They identified the exchange-rate disconnect and related puzzles that still organise the field. Their work is highly influential on exchange-rate regimes and international policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: The foundational modelling credit to Obstfeld and Rogoff is strong, as is their joint puzzles paper. Others, such as Dornbusch, Lane and Gopinath, also contributed. The pairing is coherent and intellectually natural.
assessment.maturity: The work spans the 1980s to the 2000s and is well established and widely taught. It has been long recognised and has had time to prove durable.
uncertainties: Some of the puzzles are still unresolved, which could be read as weakening the claim of a settled framework.
Rogoff is also credited in a separate financial-crisis candidacy, which makes the scope of his claim a matter of judgement.
The effect on policy is more diffuse than for the empirical or methodological candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Grossman-Helpman work on protection for sale gave a tractable political-economy model of trade policy in which lobbying determines tariffs. It also helped bring endogenous growth and innovation into trade theory. Together, these have shaped both theory and empirical work on trade agreements and special interests.
assessment.attribution: The protection-for-sale and innovation-and-growth-in-the-global-economy contributions are strongly and jointly credited to Grossman and Helpman. A two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from the early 1990s and have been tested empirically for more than two decades. Their standing is well established.
uncertainties: Empirical support for the protection-for-sale structure is mixed.
Krugman's earlier prize covered part of the new trade theory territory, so incremental novelty may be questioned.
Helpman also appears on another trade candidacy, so the relative case among trade candidates is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins modern central-bank analysis. The Taylor rule, the microfounded NK model and optimal-policy analysis have had a large and direct effect on practice, including inflation targeting and the design of monetary policy.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty because the field is crowded. Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford (NK theory and optimal policy), Galí (the NK Phillips curve and its empirics), Calvo (pricing), Gertler, Clarida, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets and Wouters all made major contributions. Any three-person subset leaves out contributors who are well known.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use at central banks. Parts of the framework were stressed by the 2021–23 inflation episode, and the question of how well it explains inflation is not fully settled.
uncertainties: The three-name cap forces arbitrary exclusions among eight credited names.
How well NK models performed in the post-pandemic inflation is debated.
Part of this territory was already recognised in earlier prizes (Lucas, Phelps, Kydland and Prescott, Bernanke).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson, Tabellini and Besley systematically brought constitutions, electoral rules, state capacity and fiscal policy into formal and empirical economics. This work created modern political economics as a field, and it explains cross-country differences in policy and outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The trio is intellectually coherent, with Persson and Tabellini's Political Economics and constitutional-design work and Besley's state-capacity and accountability work. Acemoglu, Robinson and others work in adjacent areas, but the credit for building the formal field rests most strongly with these three.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of work, a long track record and a large following. Maturity is not in question.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize recognised institutions and prosperity, which might be seen as having partly covered adjacent ground.
Possible personal or institutional ties between committee members and candidates have been disclosed but are not adjudicated here; I have not checked any specific tie.
Causal identification in some cross-country work is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work changed how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality, technology and trade exposure. It covers skill-biased technical change, the task approach to automation, and the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment. It has high policy salience and has influenced the public debate.
assessment.attribution: Katz is credited for the race-between-education-and-technology and skill-premium work, Autor for the task approach and the China-shock papers, and Hanson for the trade-shock evidence. Dorn, Acemoglu, Goldin and others made significant contributions. Credit is spread widely, and a three-person selection is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers are 20–30 years old, and the China-shock work has been debated for about a decade. The findings are still being refined.
uncertainties: Some of the China-shock magnitudes and interpretations are still contested.
Goldin's 2023 prize overlaps with the Katz-related strand.
The task framework's empirical measurement has been criticised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers model gave a non-cooperative foundation for bargaining and a unique, tractable equilibrium that links bargaining to market institutions. It underlies much applied work on wages, trade negotiation and decentralised markets. It is among the most widely used game-theoretic models.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein's 1982 model is the core contribution, and Rubinstein and Wolinsky's work extended it to markets and decentralised trade. Ståhl's earlier finite-horizon model and Binmore's work have a role, and a two-person recognition cleanly leaves out Binmore.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of impact, so confirmation and timing are not in doubt.
uncertainties: Recent prizes (2020 auctions, 2007 mechanism design, 2012 matching) mean the committee may see game and mechanism theory as already well recognised.
Experimental evidence on the alternating-offers prediction is mixed, so the theory is better known as a benchmark than as a descriptive model.
My own research is in a neighbouring area of theory, so I may overweight or underweight it; I have attempted to apply the same criteria as for other fields.
